# Chapter Two: Going Home

Shielding his eyes from the bright sun, Nero surveyed the fields that stretched as far as the eye could see, it had been many years since he had traveled from Aurtus’s Keep, the headquarters of his order and the place he had begun his journey as an embassador of the Revered Emisarry. He had forgotten how beautiful this territory could be, he had been resident in the keep of his small village for too long he reflected as he smiled over the sun-bathed fields of wheat and cotton that stretched out towards the mountains in the distance.

Nero wasn’t worried about getting too lost, the mountains were still in front of him and they had been at his back all those years ago, he was headed in the correct direction at least he thought he was, mounting his horse he easily found the market road the farmers would use to head into town and sell there harvest. Following the road, he passed farm after farm the small complexes busy as people worked the fields and took care of the animals that would make them money and feed them for the winter. There was no more noble pursuit Nero thought smiling as he passed men herding cows into a field. When he had started his quest he had been worried and vexed that the land might be under threat, but having passed the last week, seeing people working as usual and the land still the breataking beauty he remembered, he had begun to forget the urgency and horror that he and the mage had witnessed causing them to report to there perspective Order’s. Korlin and he had split ways a week ago, the Mage heading towards the east to the Order that he served. While Nero continued south towards the range of mountains that stretched across his current horizon. He had been feeling more relieved the further he rode, smiling as he followed the farmers fence, knowing this would lead him to town, he came over a ridge and the smile died on his face.

Surveying the area in front of him, he could see the smoke pillars rising into the sky, squinting he saw the wall of the village a mile out, but something wasn’t right, the smoke pire’s were coming from within the wall he thought. No that couldn’t be right, maybe they are simply clear cutting he thought, speeding up the horse as he rode. This is deja vue he thought pushing his legs faster as he tried to get to the small village that like others he had seen, even recently stood burning. “What is she hoping to prove” he asked no one, anger replacing the worry the Empress had gone too far, her mages had gone too far he reflected finally making it to the gate of the village, stopping short he soon realized that there was no reason to have bothered. Looking at the courtyard of the village a scaffolding had been erected and the pile of bodies next to those still left hanging told the story, the troops seeing this village as uncontrollable had hung the entire residents. Nero pulled off the cloak he wore to combat the cold evenings covering the small body of the child who looked no more then four. What could a four year old have possibly done to threaten these men of war he thought, the tears streaming down his face. Nero let out a scream of rage as these faces were added to the others that now made his consciousness home. “How dare you” he screamed to the sky “Why wouldn’t you save this child, or this child, or this one” he said pointing out the small limp bodies strewn between those of the adults. “What could we have ever possibly done to earn the displeasure so severe that these children had to pay the price” screaming he moved around searching the sky, looking for any sign that he could be heard. The Empress had gone too far, she had gotten the mages to aid her. How many villages he wondered were out there just like this, that they had decided to make an example of. Decided the young and the innocent needed to die to fuel the cause they used to motivate themselves to these means. Whats ends could possible be worth this he wondered. Tears now freely streaming down his face.

Nero dropped to his knees, surrounded by the corpses of these people who did nothing to offend the gods, nothing to spurn them, these bodies who until recently were the people who filled the keep praying to Aurtus, to ask for good crops of healthy children. “Aurtus, I don’t understand how you can do this, these people who have done nothing to you, nor to the gods you serve. How can the Empress have such a hold, I truly understand bad things happen? But this is too much my Lord, this is too much” he prayed pleading to the man he had dedicated his life to serve.

But no answer came, no sign to show him the gods were listening or that Aurtus himself had heard his prayer, so he stayed there on his knees until his legs went numb. Getting up his legs almost locked in place he finally began the process of burying the people of this village, to ensure they would have a proper burial, with each strike of the shovel into the dirt his hatred of the Empress and her mages grew, the fire stoked with the price of the dead. Nero vowed at that moment to not stop until the woman was dead, until the mages that served her were all dead, this was not the first time that mages had sought control, the church had been there to stop them and since that time they had become complacent, they no longer fielded a standing army, no longer had the weapons or the knowledge to combat those with the gift. Nero resolved to change that to the gods as his witness they would not become complacent again.

It began to dawn on him that maybe the punishment for these people wasn’t about what they had done, but instead what the church had. If his church had not disbanded the army, become lazy and complacent they could have moved against the Empress, stopped her before these horrible things had happened. But as of now, the church was as powerless as that child that now lay dead and cold on the ground he thought.

“Is that what this is my Lord, punishment for us, for those who dedicated ourselves to lead and protect these people. Is this our fault?” he asked standing in the shallow hole, his clothes covered with dirt as le leaned on the old shovel and considered this. For close to an hour he stood there, eyes closed as he thought about all he had seen and experienced and knew, knew deep in his heart that his people, the leader of the flock of those who saught guidance from the Emisarry could have been the champions who prevented this instead of victims, helpless and running.

It took Nero most of the night and half the next day to bury the bodies of these villagers, but he did it, without stopping, without rest and when he was done, he stood over the lumps of dirt that now held the village he stood in and said the words blessing there souls and asking Aurtus to receive them. Once done he rested, eating what little food he had before setting off towards Aurtus’s keep. His mind full of the contemplative thoughts of the last day. He would talk to the Lord Reagent, it was possible he could assign Nero to build the army back up, to again search the great library for the knowledge to train the soldiers and outfit them with the gear protecting them from the mages.

As the mountains grew larger the seed of hate that had nestled into his belly began to grow, the fertilizer of subjugation and death the fertilizer used so that by the time he reached the base of rock that held his orders keep, the seed had grown into a sturdy tree dripping with the blood of those slain at the hands of the Empress and her soldiers. Mages he thought Mages are the problem they give license to this travesty, they are the reason we find ourselves once again bathed in the blood of innocent people, farmers and tradesman who lived a simple existence so that the Empress may try to wrestle a little more power and a little more territory for her own hubris his mind continued. Climbing up the mountain trail towards the lights of the keep that loomed over the fields below he was so lost in his thoughts that he almost ran directly into a platoon of Empress’s soldiers camped near the base of the tall mountain. He quietly circled the encampment, using the rocks and brush as cover, from the look of the camp they had been there a while and did not look like they were going to be leaving any time soon he reflected as he saw the half completed wood buildings of bunk houses that had begun to be erected.

He carefully made his way up until he finally stood outside the large keep, watching as soldiers ran patrols around the property. The guards out front no longer wore the sword design of the Aurtus protectorate but instead had the golden lioness of the Empresss guard. Nero knew the castle well and circled around the old stone building, finaly reaching near the rear of the structure he found what he was looking for, completely unguarded was the coal entrance, a portal added in later years to make it easier to bring coal and wood directly into the kitchen area of the old stone hearth, Nero smiled as he noticed that even the patrols seemed to ignore the door altogether.

Since the door actually opened into a storage area, only those who had to carry the wood into the kitchen, knew that the large storage shelf at the back would swing in and open into the side chamber in the large complexs kitchen. The initiates and young messeners used to joke calling it the “secret entrance” but now Nero thanked Aurtus that it had been so built. He waited until the next patrol passed and then sprinted to the building, once there he threw open the building, breathing a sigh of relief when the iron lever gave easily, no lock or bar blocking and securing it. Closing the door behind him, he left his way around the old store room, but at the back he could see the light through the planks in back of the storage shelves, it took him almost ten minutes to feel around and find the latch that aloud the shelf to swing and winced as it creaked lightly as he pushed against the shelf, swinging it inward and slipping into the kitchen.

At this hour the kitchen was empty as it was well beyond dinner and breakfast wouldn’t start for a good few hours. He had a small window to slip in and out before he would be stuck within the old keep for the day. Feeling the time pressure, he quickly moved out of the kitchen and made his way along the dark hall to the servant’s staircase of the castle. He knew the patrols would use the main stairs and patrol the main foyer, since the servants quarters and staircases were well within the building and only one entrance allowed the servants to enter the complex into the servants rooms the guards didn’t waste soldiers on guarding it directly, instead opting to keep a guard on the exterioir door and anyplace that the servants areas intersected with the main complex.

He made it up the stairs and down another hall, coming to the door that would lead him into the outer foyer of the Lord Reagents Room. But he froze as he approached the door, outside sat a sleeping soldier. He stood there looking at the soldier, he didn’t know wether to flee, hide or continue and for a few moments stood there frozen in indecision. After a few moments Nero was embolded by the slow rising and lowering of the young soldier’s chest as he slept deeply. Carefully he approached, coming to stand next to the young soldier as he dreamd about his love, or some wonderful adventure. Nero slowly opened the door, stopping only one as the soldier shifted in his seat. The messenger almost bolted then but the noise would have surely woken the soldier. So, there he stood waiting until he settled down and began breathing deeply once again.

Finishing openin the door he stepped through, not quite closing it in case he had to leave quickly. The door opened into the receiving chamber for the Lord Reagent the plush ornate carpet and wall decorations meant to show the status of the man you were about to meet. Nero could make out the high-quality mahogany receiving couches and tables as well as the marble top of the coffee table. Each end table had an ornate gold crystal lamp. He quietly walked across the room and slowly opened the door to the Lord Reagents private chamber.

Entering the main quarters of Lord Alber Corinth, current Lord Reagent of the Church of Wic Nero was nervous to be in the presence of Aurtus’s own emissary on earth. “Lord Corinth, My Lord are you here” he whispered. A groan came from the bed as Nero watched someone shift under the ornate red velvet covers. Walking over he came to find a sweating and pale Lord Corinth, barely conscious laying in the expensive bed. Something didn’t look right he thought and peeled back the blanket, underneath the Lord Regeant was still in his robes of office, but something didn’t look right and at first Nero nearly missed the wound in his stomack because of the deep red robes the man wore.

But then he saw it, the wound looks mortal and from the demeanor of his Lord Reagent, the man did not have long to live. “My Lord” Nero hissed trying to get the man to wake even for a moment. To have him die after Nero had come all this way would be a miserable way to fail the self-imposed mission. Corinth opened his eyes, though they were not focused “Who, wo is there” the slurred voice came. They must have drugged him, or his loss of blood was affecting his mind. Nero wasn’t sure, he was not trained as doctor and the limited knowledge he had in first aid would be no help here. Mostly the young Messener just felt helpless as he tried to get the old man to focus. “Its Messenger Nero..” he began and then suddenly the eyes focused, Corinth looked directly at him, his eyes going wide “Nero, it is you, how did you get in here, nevermind Listen, the Empress has taken the keep, they hoped to keep me around to ensure that no one was suspicios, however I managed to get a letter out to my counterpart in Dever, we received a reply that basically said, there was nothing they could do, the soldiers found the reply and realizing what I had done, well one stabbed me” he said looking down at his robes, what little energy he had seemed to be fading as his eyes began to swimp out of focus. “He stabbed me” he said again as if unable to believe someone would do that. “No help, no help is coming” he continued and that realization seemed to seal the old man’s fate and he slumped unconscious. The Empress had killed the Lord Reagent, had tried to take out the religion that supported this land. He didn’t know if dever would forward the request for assistance to Turen, to the main keep of Wic where the Emissary of Aurtus currently called home,

But he wouldn’t dare hope that Turen or Dever would lend there soldier to safe them, he knew the politics involved, there would be censure and arguments but no soldiers would enter Vicor because they were all along the border waiting for the Empress to invade. Everyone knew it was coming, only a matter of when he thought. He sat there for a long time wondering what to do finally he spotted Lord Corinth’s hand and there upon it was the ring of office, the ring that made him the authority of the church in Vicor. Nero knew he didn’t have long but paused as he thought about what to do, there were a lot og messengers older and more experienced, but the leadership of the religion was here, or had been here, if the Lord Reagent was dead, then here was no reason to keep them around. Someone had to take control, had to become the head of the order lest the order be lost. With a deep sigh and a small prayer. Nero worked the ring off of the finger of the old man, during the process Corinth had awoken again, after a moment he realized what Nero was trying to do, he first tried to pull away but he was weak and Nero held him still as he continued to work off the ring, the man, not able to do anything simply lay there crying. He knew that if Nero was taking the ring, they he thought him dead. Finally, the large gold ring came free and Nero whispered a small blessing for the man before slipping the ring into his pocket and retreating back into the receiving room. He slipped past the still sleeping guard and down the hall. It took him only about five minutes to exit the keep, with no sign of the patrol he rushed across the open ground making the brush before he heard the heavy footfalls signaling the approach of the sguard patrol.

He sped away from the keep, making his way north to rendezvous with Korlin it is possible that he may have had better success finding help within the mages order. He smiled wryly as he thought of the irony of Mages helping get rid of other mages, hell he wasn’t convinced that the mages who served the Empress weren’t with the order he thought. Was it possible that the order was in on it, that the Empress had made a deal with the once secretive leaders of the Mages order he wondered? Magic in the land had become scarce and those with it were nowhere near as powerful as in the past, but the stories he had heard of the ones serving the Empress were like the mages of old. They had power and used it easily to demonstrate their superiority, was this the inevitable outcome of the church leaving the mages alive, had the founders of the order who had hunted them down been right he wondered.

These where the thoughts that plagued his mind the further, he rode, heading north, maybe Korlin would find answers, maybe he would find help. That would answer the question he thought, if the mages were able to help put this right then they wouldn’t be involved, they would help set things right and then these thoughts would resolve themselves. Guilt wracked his system, not only had he abandoned his keep, left his people to the will of the new Lord Seer of his territory but he had then seen the horrors that now befell the land and still had not fought, had not taken a stand. Nero was a Messenger, not a warrior but surely in these times he could be both he thought, pleaded to himself to find a way to save the people, to help those who now found themselves under the boot of the Crown.

Two days later Nero found himself in an abandond barn, one he and Kolrin had found and identified as the rendezvous point so Nero saw waiting, lying in the old hay as rain pelted the old thatch roof as it leaked in more spots then It offered protection. The ornate run sat in his palm as he stared at it, looking at the beauty of the item that was the power of the office of the Lord Reagent. He had taken it from Cholrin’s finger, knew the old man was dying but now what was he to do with it he wondered. The little bit light coming through the hay loft glinted off of the gold and jewels of the crown shaped into a band. Who would lead him and his brethren through this time he thought studying the ring as these thoughts played through his head? He didn’t know if the council had lived but based on the status of the keep and what he had heard happened to all of the nobility, he thought that they were probably dead or stripped of title and lands. This was a dark time and required a leader who was not only spiritual, but also a warrior someone to save the people who even now suffered under the Empress and the Mages she commanded.

As the fourth day came and went, Nero began to get worried, his friend had not returned nor had word come to him. He had the directions to the order that Kolrin had given him, but should he go there, he was not a mage and definitely wouldn’t be welcome, what if Kolrin was trying to convince the council to help and his showing up caused problems. He was close to setting off when he heard the whistling of someone as they approached the old barn. “Kolrin” Nero whispered and ran out of the barn before even a thought and almost ran into an old who was most definitely not his friend. Stopping up short he eyed the old man, covered in mud up to his knees and the heavy pack weighted down with supplies, the dirty grey beard parted into a genuine smile as the four teeth in his mouth shown. “Hello friend, you startled me” the old man said. Nero glancing down to see that the man wasn’t armed and wasn’t reaching for weapons, so he relaxed. “My apologies my friend, I was expecting someone else” he said nodding to the old man. The man just nodded and then spied the dirty robes Nero wore his brows rose as he recognized them. “You are a messenger; I apologize I did not recognize your station” he said and bowed slightly. Nero waved him off “Where are you off to friend, I was considering heading back south and since you seem to come from that direction, might you tell me the goings on in that direction?” Nero asked, maybe this man had come in contact with Kolrin, or at the very least he could tell him if the way was safe, he thought.

The old man’s face fell as he looked back over his shoulder. “Oh, Messenger you don’t want to do that, all you will find is death and sorry” he said, just loud enough for Nero to hear. Nero lowered his head, he had known, that is all he ever found these days he thought. But that was his only option he thought, where else was he to go. The old man answered that quickly. “I am going north, the outcasts are excepting refugees, I hear the Wardens may have joined them as well Messenger, you should come, staying here will only bring death or worse” he said looking back his face a mask of sorry and worry. “The outcasts?, the wardens?” he asked, trying to understand, no one had really heard from the outcasts in decades and the Wardens served the Empress, were they now rebelling he wondered a glimmer of hope sprouting next to that tree of hate that had now blossomed into a sturdy core within his body. “They are saving those to come, you should travel my friend, we can be there in less then a week, if we travel fast” the old man said excitedly happy to have the potential of some company Nero thought. It took nero an hour to make the decision and in the end, he carved a quick note to Korlin on the main beam of the barn before grabbing what little he had and headed out with the old man.

The old man took a step forward, extending his arm “I am Gil Haverdash, farmer, entrepenuer and shop owner, or was” he said shrugging at his last. Nero took the extended arm nodding. I am Veric Nero, Messenger of Aurtus and friend” he said bowing slightly. The old man smiled wider at this “Well met messenger, it will be good to have a traveling companion” he finished as he assisted Nero in gathering his supplies and putting on his pack.

They set out for the Barrens and towards hope for the future.
